_comment: Regression guardrails for the smoke tier, checked by `spbench verify` and by CI.
These bounds guard the HARNESS, not the tools. Their job is to catch a change to
the simulator, the allele extractor or the metrics that silently moves every
number - the kind of bug that would otherwise be published as a result.
They are deliberately wide. A tool improvement should not trip them; a scoring
bug should. If a legitimate change moves a value outside its range, update the
range in the same commit and say why in the message, so the reason a published
baseline moved is always in the history.
The floor/ceiling relationships are the load-bearing part:
- naive-greedy must stay clearly below strainphase on read ARI. If it catches
up, either the dataset became trivial or the metrics stopped discriminating.
- naive-greedy must keep posting a large haplotype count. That is the
over-splitting signature the report warns readers about; if it disappears,
the baseline is no longer doing its job.
Values recorded on the smoke config with seed 0 and strainphase random_seed 0.
